clue.text: Engage staff to win popularity

definitions.meaning: to hire workers for a business
to catch on and become well liked

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms of the same phrasal verb: hiring employees, and gaining favour with the public.

clue.text: Natty manoeuvre outflanks king and despot

indicators.note: to outflank is to get round both sides, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
to manoeuvre the letters of Natty is to shift them about into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A smart military manoeuvre gets round a king and his oppressive ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natty' looks like praise for the manoeuvre, but its letters are the fodder; 'outflanks' wraps them round the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who uses power cruelly, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Bet race business involved poor living standard

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the three words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Gambling on horse races leaves someone barely scraping by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the fifteen letters of BET RACE BUSINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having only enough to stay alive is a meagre, poor standard of living.

clue.text: Trepidation about the war is implied by a white one

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the synonym for trepidation is wrapped around the other word

parts.note: trepidation means fear

explanation.surface: Cowardice over going to war is suggested by a pale token.
explanation.walkthrough: In the First World War, white feathers were handed to men out of uniform to brand them cowards, hence 'war is implied by'.
explanation.definitionFit: The white feather is the traditional emblem of cowardice, so 'a white one' stands for that plume.

clue.text: Father turns in calculation for the introduction of hi-tech

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the other

parts.note: a calculation is a computation

indicators.note: turns means the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A dad gets to grips with sums as new technology arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the father; 'in' then drops that run into the calculation just before its last five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing in computers is how high technology is introduced to an office or process.

clue.text: It puts the modest punter in a state of excitement

definitions.meaning: a small bet is what a cautious gambler places
nervously excited, all of a quiver

explanation.definitionFit: A modest wager is a small gamble, while being in a flutter means being agitated or excited.

clue.text: Magnanimous Augustus accommodates English emperor in Rome

indicators.note: accommodates means makes room for, so the short name holds the other pieces

parts.note: Gus is a short form of the name Augustus
Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: The first Roman emperor kindly hosts an English visitor and another emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Augustus looks like the emperor, but he is just a man's name in its short form; the real emperor is the one 'in Rome'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnanimous means big-hearted and liberal, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Hardly a match for the conman

definitions.text: Hardly a match for the conman

parts.words: Hardly a match for the conman
parts.note: a gullible victim offers a swindler no real contest, and a one-sided contest is a walkover

explanation.definitionFit: An easy victim is a soft target, and a contest won without effort is a walkover; both fit someone who is no match for a swindler.

clue.text: Not appearing to compensate

definitions.meaning: a performer who is off the stage set is not on view
to counterbalance or make up for

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means away from the film set; as one it means to balance out or counteract.

clue.text: A one metre target

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single metre is the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a goal or objective, the same as a target.

clue.text: Press announcement is indecent and degenerate

indicators.note: is in means is placed within the other word

parts.note: taken as written
an ad is an advertisement in the press

explanation.surface: A newspaper notice is obscene and corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text runs 'in decent' together; read as 'indecent' it looks like part of the definition, but 'is in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means morally declining, which is a synonym for degenerate.

clue.text: Cuts out dried fruit

definitions.meaning: trims away unwanted parts, as a gardener does branches

explanation.definitionFit: A gardener trims branches, and dried plums are a familiar wrinkled fruit.

clue.text: Scoring dials on a dashboard

definitions.meaning: arranging music for the parts of an orchestra
the gauges and meters of a vehicle or aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: Orchestration of a piece of music, and the set of gauges in a cockpit or car, share this name.

clue.text: Turn up the stove for Indian spinach dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, turn up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gas cooker; gas is the stove's fuel and used for the stove itself

explanation.surface: Raise the heat on the hob to cook a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reverses GAS in this down clue; it pretends to mean raising the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Saag or sag is a South Asian curry made from spinach or other leafy greens.

clue.text: Vapour used in a radical fibre product

indicators.note: used in means placed inside, so the vapour goes within the other word

parts.note: radical means basic or fundamental, which is base
a vapour is a gas

explanation.surface: Steam is employed in some extreme manufacturing of fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' signals the container; 'radical' in the sense of fundamental, as in base or basic.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagasse is the fibrous pulp left after sugar cane is crushed, used for paper and fuel.

clue.text: Young Archibald's about five, according to the records

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the boy's name goes round the numeral

parts.note: Archie is a pet form of Archibald, used for a young one, with the possessive s
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A little boy named Archibald is about five years old, according to official documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts V inside ARCHIE'S, the boy's age being a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are collections of historical documents, i.e. records.

clue.text: One who reneged on a job got fed up

parts.note: a post is a job
ate up, consumed food

explanation.surface: A worker backed out of a job because they were sick of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or cause, i.e. someone who went back on their allegiance.

clue.text: Give others ammunition in support for the chairman?

parts.note: arms are weapons, which supply a fighter like ammunition
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Supply weapons to the rest of a board in backing their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' and 'in' only link the pieces. The question mark flags the chairman as one sitting in a chair, not a company head.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest at the side of a chair supports a seated person's elbow.

clue.text: One woman in seven

indicators.note: in means the name sits inside the number word

explanation.surface: One lady among seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a woman's name, the first woman in the Bible.

clue.text: Room in which a bullet is lodged

definitions.text: in which a bullet is lodged
definitions.meaning: the part of a gun's cylinder or breech that holds the cartridge

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal room and the compartment of a firearm holding the cartridge.

clue.text: Set actress to her position opposite

indicators.note: to position is to place, so the letters are placed in a different order

explanation.surface: A director tells a performer where to stand on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' rearranges SET ACTRESS TO HER, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the other side of the road from you is opposite you.

clue.text: To fill up again is a confounded ordeal

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Refilling something is a blasted trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload is to recharge a weapon or container once more.

clue.text: Team gets runs after Samuel's mentor provides vital tonic

indicators.note: after places the team and runs behind the mentor's name

parts.note: Eli the priest raised the prophet Samuel in the Bible
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sports side gains points thanks to a coach's energising drink.
explanation.walkthrough: XI, eleven players, is a standard crossword team.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed cure-all or life-giving potion.

clue.text: This little pig went to market on foot

definitions.text: This little pig went to market on foot

parts.words: This little pig went to market on foot
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme counted on a child's toes, the first little pig is the largest digit

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme pig walks to market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This little piggy went to market' is a rhyme told while wiggling a child's toes, starting with the biggest.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's first pig is the largest digit on the foot.

clue.text: Encountered everyone in charge of industrial material

parts.note: met means encountered
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Meeting all the staff in charge of factory supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal is the industrial material, and metallic means made of or like it.

clue.text: Return of prohibition leads to arrest

indicators.note: return of means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: Bringing back the alcohol ban leads to police action.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is slang for to catch or seize a criminal.

clue.text: Sort of ulcer caused by the latest investment spasm?

parts.note: a PEP was a Personal Equity Plan, a then-new British tax-free investment
a tic is a muscular spasm

explanation.surface: Worry about a new savings scheme brings on a stomach ulcer.
explanation.walkthrough: A PEP, a Personal Equity Plan, was a British savings product of the late 1980s and 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A peptic ulcer forms in the stomach or duodenum, the sort linked to digestion.

clue.text: I am gone a bundle on myself!

definitions.text: I am gone a bundle on myself!

indicators.note: a bundle is a jumbled bunch, so the letters before it are bundled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are utterly smitten with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bundle' rearranges I AM GONE A. To have 'gone a bundle on' something is British slang for being very keen on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crazy about oneself is extreme self-obsession, a mania for the self.
